findings.title: Migration crashes on fresh or unconfigured databases when querying site_settings
findings.body:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb`, lines 9-11 and line 15 index `[0]` directly on the PG::Result returned by `execute(...)` without checking whether any rows were returned:

```ruby
category_id = execute("SELECT c.id FROM categories AS c
                    INNER JOIN site_settings AS s ON s.value = c.name
                    WHERE s.name = 'embed_category'")[0]['id'].to_i

if category_id == 0
  category_id = execute("SELECT value FROM site_settings WHERE name = 'uncategorized_category_id'")[0]['value'].to_i
end
```

If `embed_category` was never modified from its default (so no row exists in `site_settings`, or its value doesn't match a category name), the first query returns 0 rows and `[0]` raises `IndexError: tuple index 0 out of range` (or `NoMethodError` on `nil`). Similarly, on a fresh database being migrated before seeding, `uncategorized_category_id` is not in `site_settings`, causing line 15 to fail as well. Both queries need a `cmd_tuples > 0` check (like line 19 does) and a fallback when no row is found.

findings.title: Migrated embeddable_hosts are not normalized and bypass SQL escaping
findings.body:
In `db/migrate/20150818190757_create_embeddable_hosts.rb` line 25, existing `embeddable_hosts` values are inserted directly into the table via raw SQL interpolation:

```ruby
execute "INSERT INTO embeddable_hosts (host, category_id, created_at, updated_at) VALUES ('#{h}', #{category_id}, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP, CURRENT_TIMESTAMP)"
```

Previously, `SiteSetting.allows_embeddable_host?` stripped `http://` / `https://` and extracted `URI(h).host` at check time (as tested in the removed specs in `site_setting_spec.rb`), whereas `EmbeddableHost` now strips the scheme and path in a `before_validation` callback and compares `lower(host) = ?` against `uri.host`. Because the migration uses raw `INSERT` instead of the model or stripping the scheme/path/whitespace (`\r`), any existing setting stored with `http://`, `https://`, a path, or trailing `\r` will be inserted verbatim and will fail to match in `EmbeddableHost.record_for_host`.

findings.title: `before_validation` raises NoMethodError when `host` is nil
findings.body:
In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lines 5-8, the `before_validation` callback calls `self.host.sub!` unconditionally:

```ruby
before_validation do
  self.host.sub!(/^https?:\/\//, '')
  self.host.sub!(/\/.*$/, '')
end
```

If an `EmbeddableHost` is validated when `host` is `nil` (for example, `EmbeddableHost.new.valid?` or a request with missing `host` param), `self.host.sub!` raises `NoMethodError: undefined method 'sub!' for nil:NilClass` instead of failing validation cleanly.

findings.title: `record_for_host` fails to match when the input URL has an uppercase hostname or non-standard port
findings.body:
In `app/models/embeddable_host.rb` lines 10-18:

```ruby
def self.record_for_host(host)
  uri = URI(host) rescue nil
  return false unless uri.present?

  host = uri.host
  return false unless host.present?

  where("lower(host) = ?", host).first
end
```

1. `URI(url).host` preserves the case of the input string in Ruby (e.g., `URI('http://EvilTrout.com/foo').host == 'EvilTrout.com'`). Comparing `lower(host) = ?` against an un-downcased `host` parameter will never match if the referer/embed URL contains any uppercase characters in the hostname (`host.downcase` should be used).
2. The format regex on line 2 explicitly allows ports (e.g., `example.com:8000`), which get saved in the `host` column, but `uri.host` strips the port, so any `EmbeddableHost` saved with a port will never be matched by `record_for_host`.

findings.title: Fabricator definitions are swapped between `category_fabricator.rb` and `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb`
findings.body: The contents of `spec/fabricators/category_fabricator.rb` and `spec/fabricators/embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` are inverted: `category_fabricator.rb` now defines `Fabricator(:embeddable_host)`, while `embeddable_host_fabricator.rb` defines `Fabricator(:category)` and its variants.

findings.title: Misleading spec description and setup in `expandable_first_post?`
findings.body:
In `spec/models/topic_spec.rb` lines 1403-1405:

```ruby
it "is false if embeddable_host is blank" do
  expect(topic.expandable_first_post?).to eq(false)
end
```

`Topic#expandable_first_post?` no longer checks `EmbeddableHost` at all (`SiteSetting.embed_truncate? && has_topic_embed?`). In this test, neither `SiteSetting.embed_truncate` nor `has_topic_embed?` is set, so it returns `false` regardless of whether an `embeddable_host` exists.
